utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If we could have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Buja. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, it still applies. Mr. Whiting will continue with his questions now. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Buja.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you understand me clearly?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll remind you for the benefit of the interpreters, who have to translate what you say, if you could try at all times to speak up, that would be appreciated. Do you understand? Thank you. When we stopped yesterday I believe that you told us in March and April of 1998 you were in Mullapolc and you were organising in the municipalities of Lipjan and Shtime. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to -- with the assistance of the usher, I'm going to show you a map. It's map 6 from Prosecution Exhibit 1, and if it could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We have a copy of it because he'll mark it. I think it has to be turned the other way. It's upside down -- or at least within the computers it's upside down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, if you could look at the map on your left. I know it appears on the screen, but if you could look at the map on your left. Can you find, first of all, your home village, Bujan, on the map? Do you see it? Could you take a pen and just circle that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Maybe if the map could be pushed over a little bit so it appears on the screen. A little more. If that could be brought to the centre of the -- there we go. And if the record could reflect that the witness has circled the dot which is next to "Bujan" on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And now where is Mullapolc?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the witness has circled the dot next to Mullapolc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, during this time in March and April of 1998 you said you were organising in Lipjan and Shtime. Were you organising in any particular villages?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the villages. The units were for the municipality of Shtime and Lipjan. I thought that we had to organise a guerrilla unit as instructions were from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. And during March and April of 1998 did you stay in Mullapolc during those two months?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed with the family of Ahmet Mujoci.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this map be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P157.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can take the map away for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Buja, during those two months, March and April of 1998, what exactly you were doing. You've told us you were organising guerrilla units but can you tell us what you did day to day to accomplish that task.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time we were in profound illegality. My brother, Rame Buja, was supposed -- I ordered him actually to contact me with people in Lipjan so that I could start talks with them regarding the political and military aspect of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I -- we did that. Even though it was not an easy task to contact the people because, as I said earlier, we were in profound illegality. It took me several days to establish contacts with two or three people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember any of those people that you established contacts with?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I contacted initially with Huset Sahiti, then Besim Rrustemi and then Fitim Rustemi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, when you say Lipjan, these people in Lipjan, do you mean Lipjan the town or Lipjan the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was the result of these talks that you had with these individuals that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sahiti was a former political prisoner. He had to work in the former Ministry of Defence of the government of Bujar Bukoshi and I believe he had experience regarding these organisations. So the talks with him were easier because he was a man who understood the significance of this organisation and he was willing to do something in this respect, that is the military organisation of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And so did you do anything? Was anything done as a result of these discussions?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in March and April. That was impossible to organise a unit. I thought it would take me at least six months to do so, but later things developed so fast -- you know, the protest staged by the Albanian population in March and April in support of the KLA after the heroic war of the legendary commander and the sublime sacrifice made by his family, Jashari family. So events rolled so fast -- faster than I thought to implement directives of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the directives of the General Staff, what are you referring to exactly, implementing the directives? Are you referring to what you testified about yesterday, that is the instructions you received through Hashim Thaqi in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During -- so aside from having these discussions with these individuals during March and April, did you do anything else to organise units in Lipjan and Shtime municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. March and April were mostly months where we -- when we established contacts, when we would more or less figure out the structure of the guerrilla units. So all the talks we held at that time were done in order to find out whether the people I was contacted were willing to organise in the guerrilla unit that I thought start operation [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in your -- in this phase, March and April when you were establishing contacts and figuring out the structure, were you doing this in coordination with anybody outside of Lipjan and Shtime?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was doing this in cooperation with Rame Buja who established those contacts because at the time we were kind of independently operating, if I may so -- if I might say so, regarding the organisation of the guerrilla unit. Actually we were trying to organise the people we thought we knew well regarding their patriotic activity. That was our underlying motive, to contact them and agree on the structure. But we suffered great loss -- shortages of armaments at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in March and April did you have any -- were you doing these tasks -- were you cooperating in any way or coordinating in any way with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in April - I don't remember the date - through the courier, my courier, my brother, Avni Buja, I tried to contact Fatmir Limaj so that I could go to Klecka to contact the General Staff through Hashim Thaqi in Drenica to tell them about the organisation efforts I was making and the shortage of arms, which had become a must. And we were unable to find weapons. So we started to contact people to talk with them and were kind of determined about -- we knew about the people who would be involved in the organisation in Lipjan and Shtime, but shortages of weapons prevented us. So my purpose was to go to Klecka physically and then to be accompanied to Drenica, but this contact was not made possible due to the disagreements between the two couriers; or to put it better, because of their failure to know exactly where the meeting place would be in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall if this was at the beginning of April or at the end of April, middle of April?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been in the first part of April because in the second half or at the end of April I went to Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you go to Klecka in the second half of April?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of my trip there was what I said earlier, and the failure of that meeting made me go there nevertheless and from there start for Drenica. What I thought I could meet Mr. Thaqi. But the large concentration of Serb forces on the Peja-Pristina road as well as the great movements of the police along that road, the great danger facing us to penetrate Drenica, prevented me from going to Drenica from Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed the night there and on the next day I met a man who had come from Germany; his name is Imri Ilazi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then what happened? That next day what happened? Did you leave Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day it was impossible for us to move because we were afraid of being detected by the Serb forces. So mainly we moved in the night. So I waited for the night to fall and together with Imri Ilazi we left for Mullapolc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you were in Klecka for two nights?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One night and one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on the second night you left?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see Fatmir Limaj there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with him?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did -- what did you discuss with him?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly our talks focused on political issues and military issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ask him to make contact with the General Staff on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on my behalf. I didn't ask him to do that. But we talked about the difficulties of making contacts with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you make any plan or discuss any plan for him to make contact with the General Staff to get information for you, for your tasks?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you learn what he was doing in Klecka at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw there was a small number of soldiers there and they were guarding the village, Klecke village, and where we were staying in the house of Fatmir Limaj's nephews.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if that group of soldiers had a name, a unit name for example?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I don't recall that unit to have had a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You say "at that time." Did you -- did there come a time later when you learned that unit to have a name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later yes of course. I learned the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in May I think. The name of the unit changed -- I mean became Celiku Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did it -- did it have a number, the unit in Klecka, Celiku with a number, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say in full certainty, but as far as I remember it was Celiku 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you spent a night in Klecka, you returned the following night to Mullapolc. What happened when you returned to Mullapolc?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trip to Mullapolc was not for one night because it was difficult to get there in a night, but after we arrived there on the second night I of course started to think about the organisational issues together with Imri Ilazi regarding the Ferizaj unit in order to make contacts with people regarding the guerrilla unit for Ferizaj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So now in addition to organising in Shtime and Lipjan, you're organising in Ferizaj municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the Ferizaj municipality it was Imri Ilazi who started the work of organisation of this unit, but being there with him in Mullapolc, I helped him in this task to make contacts with people that we both knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What about the municipality of Kacanik? Was there any work being done to organise there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. With the arrival of Agim Bajrami work started there as in all other municipalities, as in my municipality. Even though Agim Bajrami had been making greater progress in Kacanik municipality with respect to the organisation of the guerrilla unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you yourself get involved in organising in the Kacanik municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period of March and April I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In a later period did you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my arrival in Kacanik, which was made possible thanks to the organisation of Imri Ilazi in Ferizaj municipality, I could travel up to Kacanik because Imri Ilazi and the people he had started organising knew the terrain. So I contacted Agim Bajrami in Kacanik municipality. If I'm not mistaken, there was in Duraj village. And during that meeting we discussed the same issues, that is that I had discussed with Fatmir, about political and military aspects. In that case Agim Bajrami explained to me that just like me he, too, faced shortages of arms and munitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meeting was held in May. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Beginning of May or end of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was -- the meeting was in the beginning of May, but my stay there in the Kacanik municipality lasted quite -- for a considerable time. And so this Honourable Chamber should know that the trip lasted for days, not for hours, because from Mullapolc to Kacanik municipality or to the part we went later, Gllobocice, is a very hard trip, a trip that lasts many nights. It's a very rugged terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You told us that after you were in Klecka you went back at the end of April 1998 you went back to Mullapolc. Were you in Mullapolc until you went to Kacanik at the beginning of May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long do you think you stayed in Kacanik when you went at the beginning of May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact figure, but including the trip and my stay there together with Agim Bajrami lasted 15 days -- 10 or 15 days I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you map 4 from Prosecution Exhibit 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if that could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, this is a map of the municipalities as they existed in 1998. Can you just circle the municipalities that we've been talking about, Lipjan, Shtime, Ferizaj, Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Lipjan -- the Lipjan municipality is here; Shtime, which is a small municipality; Ferizaj municipality; and Kacanik municipality. I can see them in this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if you could -- and is that how you remember the municipalities existing at the time in 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure because I see only the names of the municipalities and maybe some villages were not very precisely included in these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, I just mean the general shape and location of the municipalities; is that how you remember them?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is more or less how the shape I think has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just so we have a good record, if you could just take a pen and circle those four municipalities, just the names of those four.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If that could be given a number, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it can be taken off the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, did you -- I believe you testified that Imri Ilazi was organising in Ferizaj. Did you in this time period - now we're moving forward to April, May 1998 - did you spend any time in Ferizaj municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Ferizaj municipality through the villages of Jezerce, Vineredime [phoen], and Buca highlands, Greme village. Then we went to the villages of Kacanik, Duraj, and during my stay in Kacanik we went up to Gllobocice, which lies in the border with Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said that you had discussions with Agim Bajrami that were similar to the discussions you had had with Fatmir Limaj about organising in Kacanik. Did you have similar discussions with Imri Ilazi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had almost the same talks. We had the same concerns because they were the concerns of all of us at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And again I'm going to ask you the same question I asked you before when we were talking just about March and April. Now we're talking about May and we're talking about other municipalities. Did you -- did you coordinate your organisation activities in these municipalities and with these other people with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordination of our activity did not continue up to May, but in May, as I said earlier, after the contact I made with Hashim Thaqi via telephone I undertook to take care of the transportation, the shipping of arms from Albania to Kosova. I undertook to coordinate the activity of Kacanik unit, Ferizaj, Shtime, Lipjan in order to take care of the supply line. That was the supply line for weapons, ammunitions. That was the task I was given by the General Staff, Hashim Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when was that in May that you made direct contact with Hashim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a direct contact; it was through the telephone which happened during my visit in Kacanik. The contact was made after the information we received from our collaborator Agush Buja and Adem Grabovci, who informed us that Hashim Thaqi was in Switzerland. So we insisted, that is myself and Agim Bajrami, to contact him through the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you've testified that you made direct contact and coordinated directly with Hashim Thaqi about creating a supply line for weapons and ammunitions for the municipalities that you were now organising or were participating in organising, Kacanik, Ferizaj, Shtime, and Lipjan. Did you also coordinate with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I already said that I have had contacts by telephone, not direct contacts. And before this telephone contact I did not coordinate, did not organise these units because every -- each and every one of these units had a person in charge. In Kacanik it was Agim Bajrami responsible for that; in Ferizaj it was Imri Ilazi; for Shtime and Lipjan it was myself. So this means that up to the period when I was tasked to coordinate, this was specific task to coordinate the activity of the units regarding the supply -- the armament supply line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And my question is: Did this task come from Hashim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was conveyed to me by Hashim Thaqi. It was -- that was the belief that at that time that the General Staff tasks you to create the supply line for armaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday that when you were tasked by Hashim Thaqi in March of 1998 and you -- in Drenica that it was specific to Lipjan and Shtime. Did there come a point where your task was expanded to include Kacanik and Ferizaj; that is, were you told at some point that your task was broader and it would include Kacanik and Ferizaj?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an extra task, a specific task, to coordinate the activities of Kacanik, Ferizaj, Shtime, Lipjan units to create this weapons supply line. That was an extra responsibility for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did you learn of that extra responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in May during my visit to Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But did you take on this extra responsibility on your own or were you assigned this extra responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If I was not willing to take up this responsibility, it wouldn't have been assigned to me. I was ready to act and work according to the orders issued by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who communicated to you that you would have this extra responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find this insisting a little bit strange. I was clear when I said that the communication was made with Hashim Thaqi by phone regarding this extra work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. I think I understand now, and that communication was in May of 1998 before you went to Kacanik or when -- I'm sorry, when you were in Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Aside -- just so we're clear, aside from your communication with Hashim Thaqi, which you've described, by telephone, and your contacts with the leaders of the units that you have talked about, Agim Bajrami and Imri Ilazi, did you coordinate with anybody else in these activities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, my task was very specific. It was clear to me that my job was to coordinate the units in Shtime and Lipjan in order to establish this weapons supply route. It wasn't more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, let's move forward. After you had this communication with Hashim Thaqi in May and you had this plan to establish this weapons supply route, what happened next? What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During those days in Kacanik together with Agim Bajrami, we tried to divide the tasks regarding this weapons supply route. Agim Bajrami's unit take up -- took up the responsibility to escort the weapons that were coming from Albania and Macedonia. And as for Greme village, this task was to be carried out by the Ferizaj unit and then to be passed to another unit in my municipality where I was responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you able to set up a weapons supply route?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In agreement with Agim Bajrami and Imri Ilazi, we did not take the risk to have only one supply route because it was a dangerous time in Kosovo so that this supply route could be very easily cut. So therefore, we left the so-called reserve lines. There were two additional reserve supply lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you've made references a number of times to units, the Ferizaj unit, a unit in your municipality where you were responsible. Were these units groups of soldiers under your command and under the command of Agim Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These units were guerrilla units which at that time had instructions -- we had instructions at that time by -- from the General Staff to create and establish these guerrilla units. In Kacanik there existed the Kacanik unit which was led by Agim Bajrami. In Ferizaj the unit was created a little bit later in the end of April/beginning of May and the leader was Imri Ilazi. While in Shtime it wasn't created yet. The weapons that were expected to arrive through this supply line were being waited [as interpreted]. And this unit was led by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that unit that was led by you in Shtime created?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit was created after the weapons arrived together with me from Kacanik to Lipjan municipality, more exactly in the village of Kroimire. The reason why it was Kroimire was that there were two other soldier who had arrived there from Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrival in Kroimire occurred in the end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who were the two soldiers from Germany that were there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Qeriqi, who was later known with the pseudonym Luani, and another soldier whose name was Fadil, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did -- was Fadil the other soldier's name or pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether it was his name or pseudonym, but I knew him simply as "Fadil" because he was in Kroimire and he came from the village of Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever learn his real -- any other name for him, whether it be pseudonym or other name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the person who I knew at that time as Fadil I mentioned yesterday at that time it was illogical to ask whether it was his real name or pseudonym because this could put him and his family and soldiers in risk. Therefore, I just knew him as "Fadil" and I couldn't ask him if that was his name or pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, but my question was: Did you later learn a name or pseudonym for him? Did you later learn information about who this Fadil is?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even today I call him Fadil. I don't know whether he -- it is his real name or pseudonym. It can happen even now after the war for us to call soldiers with their names that they used in the war, and without knowing whether it was a pseudonym or a real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kroimire at the end of May 1998 you said there were these two soldiers from Germany there, Ramiz Qeriqi and Fadil. What did you find there in Kroimire? Was anything organised?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see much of an organisation, but according to Ramiz Qeriqi he had spoken with the people who were ready for engagement. Therefore, the weapons that I brought from Kacanik through that supply line that I mentioned the soldiers from Kroimire and from the Kroimire area were equipped with those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said that you then commanded this unit. Did this unit have a name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these persons got weapons, the meeting that was held, in this meeting it was decided that this guerrilla unit took up the name of Sokoli.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did that name come from, Sokoli?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokoli is a bird. In Albanian it's name is "petriti" and therefore we found this name suitable for our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many days, but I know it was several days. We made an effort to get even better organised as Sokoli Unit, although this unit as a name was not known. The Serb forces that were coming from the direction of Petrastica in those villages made us organise in Pjetershtice as well. After this unit came into existence in Kroimire, there was a flux of people who were ready to join the KLA and this made us think of expansion and formation of new units. But there was shortage of weapons and I was forced to go Kacanik again in order to organise the weapons supply, to make it function better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said that the Sokoli Unit was based in Kroimire but expanded to Petrastica. Did it also expand to Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this made us think as Sokoli Unit to actually create another unit in Pjetershtice, and this happened really fast because the flux of people was great. They were even coming with their own weapons. So it was possible to create even a smaller unit in Pjetershtice. Honoured Judges, here we should take into consideration how -- the way things developed. This was very fast. Changes happened on daily basis, the flux of people and their pressure to join the KLA. Therefore the unit that was formed in Pjetershtice expanded really fast. New soldiers enrolled, and it became a bigger guerrilla unit that -- than we actually expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But did you also expand to Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it earlier that Sokoli Unit did not function later on. It was not known as Sokoli Unit because part of its soldiers led by Ramiz Qeriqi, they settled in Pjetershtice where they formed a new unit. Maybe this marks a beginning of certain problems that we had regarding the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The new unit that settled in Petrastica, did it have a different name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not called Sokoli Unit but it was called after the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. village, the Petrastica Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was in charge of that unit, the Petrastica Unit?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on several days later the Petrastica Unit covered the areas of Zborce and the person in charge was Ramiz Qeriqi, known as Luani. Several days in a row I went there to give my suggestions regarding their positions, but problems came into existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What kind of problems -- did you have problems with Commander Luani?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These problems were mainly in regard to organisation issues. I was for an organisation which would be done step by step and for respecting the rules of the KLA. This caused us not to be in good terms with each other. That person, to my opinion, was quite anarchic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So the -- you remained in command of the unit in Kroimire. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kroimire at that time there were three or four soldiers and there was a person, one soldier, who dealt with the registration of persons who came to Kroimire to express their willingness to engage and contribute to the ranks of the KLA. My task regarding the weapons supply for the Shtime-Kacanik-Lipjan route and the flux of people who wanted to join the KLA forced me to take the journey to Kacanik again after several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You returned to Kacanik; how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This period, namely the period I'm speaking of at this moment, the beginning of June, was a time of better organisation regarding the Kacanik and Ferizaj units. The journey to Kacanik was easier and faster. In Kacanik it was possible for me to go within two nights and to stay there for a day or two and then come back and the entire journey to take me around six or seven days in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you then return to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I returned to Kroimire with several weapons that I obtained through this supply line from Gllobocice and the unit of Agim Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Kroimire when you returned on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my return to Kroimire, the thing that we were waiting for a long time happened, the public appearance of the KLA spokesperson who gave his first statement. This made us be more aware and made us -- made it possible for us to communicate with the General Staff through Jakup Krasniqi, the spokesperson; this happened in mid-June. During this time I was this Kroimire, but after the public appearance of Jakup Krasniqi, I insisted to meet the spokesperson of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met him after the 15th or 16th. I remember this date due to the engagement of my brother, Rame Buja, in the ranks of the KLA. I met with Jakup Krasniqi in Klecka. He was there for an interview. We discussed with him the possibilities for organising ourselves better in the parts where I had contacts. Simply, Jakup Krasniqi at that time informed me that the subzones of the KLA had been designated and that those days one or two commanders of subzones were appointed. And he also told me that he planned to organise and appoint commanders of another subzone whose name -- which name he didn't know but this subzone was to include the municipalities of Shtime and Ferizaj. The dilemma at that time was the municipalities of Kacanik and Elez Hani. This information motivated me to work even harder and on that day Jakup Krasniqi had an interview. Some journalists wanted to interview him and myself, together with Jakup Krasniqi, would be on that interview. And of course the interview was given by the spokesperson while I was standing at his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that's the 15th or 16th. Is that the 15th or 16th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this happened after 15th or 16th of June, and I remember these dates due to the engagement of my brother. To my recollection, he got engaged with a weapon in the KLA on the 16th. Now, after these dates, I don't know when exactly it happened but it was around the 20th of June. So this is an approximate date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, we'll return to those subjects later, but I want to focus now on the time period from May till the middle of June. You told us before that at the end of April you went to Klecka and spent one night there. And now you've told us that around the 20th of June you met with Jakup Krasniqi in Klecka. Between those two dates, between the end and April and the middle of June, did you go to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It was a long question. Between -- from the end of April until the middle of June 1998 did you go to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it could have been at some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when it could have been?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been the time in Kroimire while I was staying in Kroimire. Maybe it was early June; I cannot give the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember why you went to Kroimire -- I mean Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply to visit my comrades, to meet Fatmir Limaj and Ismet Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you meet Fatmir Limaj and Ismet Jashari?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you describe the nature of your meetings with them? What happened? What was the purpose of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the purpose of these meetings was to see my comrades whom I hadn't seen for some time just to find out how they were doing. It was just a social meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from that occasion which was just a social meeting, did you have -- do you recall any other trips to Klecka during that time period from the end of April to the middle of June 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember another meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During that same time period from the end of April to the middle of June 1998, did you have any other forms of communication with Fatmir Limaj, by courier, by telephone, by any other means? I'm not sure if you answered, but it didn't -- nothing was picked up.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. If you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I will. From the end -- you've told us that at some point at the beginning of June you made a social trip to Klecka, and that was the only trip you made to Klecka. Did -- let -- I'll take this -- I'll ask a different question first. During that time period, end of April to the middle of June 1998, did you see Fatmir Limaj anywhere else aside from Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him somewhere else. I remember seeing him in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During that same time from the end of April to the middle of June 1998, did you communicate with Fatmir Limaj any other way by, for example, by telephone or by courier?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I stressed earlier through a courier sometime in April, end of April, it was then when I contacted with Fatmir Limaj. But the later period, as I explained it earlier, I was in Mullapolc and then went to Kacanik. And during this period, we could not contact by any other means of contact, by any means of contact at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But how about when you were in Kroimire? Did you have any contact by telephone or by courier during -- from the end of April until the middle of June 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this earlier. I was in Kroimire in end of May and I know that I met once with him. I know that I went to Klecka in beginning of June. As for other occasions when I met him, I do not remember those occasions. It is possible that I met him, but I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I take it that you had no communication by courier. Aside from that attempted communication at the end of April, you had no communication by courier during the time period I've been talking about, end of April to the middle of June 1998? I just need a clear answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a clear answer earlier. You should take into consideration what I just said. In end of April after meeting with Fatmir Limaj I settled in Mullapolc and it wasn't possible for me to have contacts with Fatmir Limaj until the -- my return from Kacanik. Of course after the return from Kacanik we came out to -- publicly with a unit in Kroimire. In June for several days, I was in Kroimire and to my recollection I contacted Fatmir Limaj once in Klecka where I went for a visit to visit Fatmir Limaj and Ismet Jashari; this is my direct contact with them which I remember. As for other contacts, it is possible that we have met during a battle or fighting, but I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I -- you've been very clear about your direct contacts and your testimony has been very clear. What I'm asking you is whether you had any telephone contact or any courier contact when you were in -- you said that wasn't possible in Mullapolc but when you were in Kroimire in May and June -- first half of June 1998. And if you could just focus on that question: Any telephone or courier contacts between May and the first part of June 1998 with Fatmir Limaj? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During June I didn't have a phone, I didn't have a radio. Therefore, contacts with Fatmir Limaj via communication means were lacking. I didn't have contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the -- Kroimire where the unit was -- the Sokoli Unit was based, did -- did -- well, let me ask a slightly different question. Were the places that units were based, for example, like Kroimire where the Sokoli Unit was based, did those places have a name, were they referred to by -- by a name, for example a headquarters or some other name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period we cannot speak of a staff. I understand very well what a staff is. Honoured Judges, under "staff" I believe that it should have its commander and a good structure, which we lacked at that time. It was a pure guerrilla unit which had a commander and sometimes a deputy commander. At that time the existence of a staff was not possible the way you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think you're anticipating a question that I haven't asked. My question is: Was the place referred to by any name, headquarters, any other name?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place was called Kroimire. The guerrilla unit initially was called Sokoli. Then afterwards it was disbanded another -- and the unit was formed in Pjetershtice, the unit that we then called Zborce unit. At a later phase another unit was formed in Blinaje and Fushtice, but the units were called after the villages where they were set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the term "point" or "post"?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have heard it, even though it was not -- did not carry any military conation, it was not a military expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How was it used, the term point or "pika"?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear what points you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, for example, was Kroimire ever referred to as a point? You said there was a unit at Fustica. Was that ever referred to as a point?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the way the soldiers refers to them. In Fushtice there was a firing line. When the guerrilla unit had to engage in a frontal war, that line was called as the fire line. Maybe they called -- the soldiers called it "point." I cannot be very precise, but what I know is that we referred to it as a fire line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is -- I'll put it this way: Was Kroimire -- did you ever hear Kroimire referred to as a point or Petrastica as a point?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm here to testify to what I know and I've seen. I am saying that I know that there have been fire lines. There have been guerrilla units which were named after the villages they were formed. As to what people called them, what words they used to describe them, I'm here under oath and wish to tell here what I knew and know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that answer no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer is I didn't know, I didn't hear. Simply, I don't know. I know about the fire lines, but as to how others described them I'm not here to testify to what others have said but to what I myself have seen and can say here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were asked whether you had heard the term, and I gather that your answer is no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from you -- we'll refer to it then as units and not points. Aside from units being established in Kroimire and you referred to Fustica, did you become aware of other villages in this area around Kroimire where units were established during this time period in May and June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the units I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you repeat them for me, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of Pjetershtice, the units of Zborce, the units of Blinaje, the unit of Fushtice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were these all established in May and June of -- May and early June 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of May, as I said earlier, the first unit was set up in Kroimire; the other units were formed in June. So the establishment of these units was not done overnight; it took days. And it -- they were formed gradually. The units of Pjetershtice and Zborce were formed earlier; later the Blinaje unit was formed. And several days later, which for us it was rather late considering the need for organisation, was that of Fushtice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were all those units -- by the time you met with Jakup Krasniqi in Klecka around the 20th of June, 1998, were all those units formed?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. The Blinaje unit was formed and later that of Fushtice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What about in Luznica? Did you hear about a unit being formed in Luznica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Luznica to visit the unit at a later phase, and it was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. -- there was a guerrilla unit in there, in Luzhnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that? When you visited, when was that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the end of June/beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you visited did you learn that there was a unit in Luznica? When I say "learn," I mean were you told, did you hear? Did you somehow come to know that there was a unit in Luznica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had understood that there were soldiers in Luznica, but I learned that there was a unit when I visited Luzhnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did you unit that there were soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Luzhnice it was after my return from Kacanik, in June I think. It was then that I realised that the -- there are soldiers in Luzhnice, and then after my visit I realised it was a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the first morning break now, resuming at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, before we broke you told us that there was a unit in Luznica, that you learned this at the end of June/beginning of July 1998. How about in Lapusnik? Were you aware of a unit being in Lapusnik? During May or June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there were several units in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you know this?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my return from Kacanik, of course, at the end of May/beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that because we acted in Kroimire, Shale, Nekovce, which was in the territory of the units that were being formed in Fustica and Blinaje. And I had heard about the fighting that had started in the Lapusnik gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was, the fighting in Lapusnik gorge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date but it was in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened after the fighting in Lapusnik gorge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the fighting from what I heard the Lapusnik gorge was blocked by the guerrilla units of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was a unit or units formed then in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure, but I heard that there were some units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear the names of the units?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of several units like the unit Pellumbi, Guri, Celiku 3. If I'm not wrong, the unit Lumi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The -- are you aware that Lapusnik is divided by the Peja-Pristina road?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very little Lapusnik as a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But are you aware it is divided in two by that road?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Lapusnik is divided in two parts or whether it's one part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The -- you referred to the Celiku 3 unit. Do you know where specifically, what part of Lapusnik that was located in?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically because I did not operate in Lapusnik. So it's hard for me to tell you exactly where this unit operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you give us any information about where -- you said you can't do it exactly or specifically. Can you give us any information about where the Celiku 3 unit operated in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- I cannot give any information. I can only say that from what I knew the Celiku 3 was located in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you're unable to give anymore information than that about where in Lapusnik it operated?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know that because I was operating in another part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How about the Guri unit? Do you have any information about where specifically that unit operated?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard, even though I'm not here about what I heard, since you are insisting I may tell you that the Guri unit operated, as I said earlier, in the Lapusnik region or area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But do you have anymore information aside from that? And I am, to be clear, asking what you heard, what you saw, what you learned. Do you have any other information about where the Guri unit operated, aside from Lapusnik? Any more specific information?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't wish to speak about what I have heard after the war because we have often talked about the war after the war, looking at it from the angle of a post-war time and not from the angle of what it was at that time. At that time I knew about units that existed or operated in Lapusnik. I knew about the units that I mentioned earlier, the Guri unit, Pellumbi, Celiku 3, and if I'm not mistaken, Lumi unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is at the time you didn't know anything more specific about where these units operated. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How about Javor? Was there a unit in Javor?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that there was a unit in Javor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you about your knowledge of what commanded various units. You've already told us about Kroimire. How about Luznica, the unit in Luznica, who commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my visit there I met with Ismet Jashari, who seemed to be the commander of the unit in Luzhnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Ismet Jashari is -- was he known at that time by his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was known by the pseudonym Kumanova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the Celiku 3 unit in Lapusnik, do you know who commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know who commanded Celiku 3 unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you've described units in May and June of 1998 in various places, in Kroimire, Petrastica, Fustica, Lapusnik, Luznica, and other places. My question is: Was there any command or coordination above these units at that time in May/June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to explain to you that the Kosova Liberation Army grew according to several stages, and prior to March 1998 it was in extreme illegality. After March it was restricted I would say or limited, illegality. It was semi-legal, I would say. It was the phase of the development of the guerrilla units in June/July. It was a phase that developed very rapidly. I might describe it as a horizontal development in terms of the KLA units. We combined the guerrilla warfare with the frontal war, which was being applied for the first time in the history of the wars in Kosova. This combination, which is known in the guerrilla warfare as an invincible unit - that hits and withdraws very quickly, whereas the front is always known through the regular military formations units - this combination which seemed very successful in June/July led us to have heavy guerrilla units that operated through frontal warfare, taking up positions. This was done because we were afraid of possible massacres and the need to defend the civilian population. This period is characterised by guerrilla units that are very quickly organised in some instances. They -- the soldiers of these units or the commanders didn't know of other -- the existence of other guerrilla units. This prompted us to try to coordinate their actions for them not to get out of control. This coordination of the units was done -- was necessary especially when we were fighting because the Serb forces attacked a guerrilla unit, and the other guerrilla units went to its rescue. At a later phase the leaders of the Serb forces probably understood this tactic, and in July they attacked us in all the firing points, in all the frontal lines where the guerrilla units had taken up positions. In June when -- after contacts with Jakup Krasniqi I began to organise the operational subzone of Nerodime which would include Lipjan, Shtime, Ferizaj towns and we were discussing Kacanik and Elez Hani. I began to coordinate the actions of the units that were in Lipjan municipality, to coordinate, to better arm them and supply them with munitions, and give instructions to them to take better positions. It was at that time that I began the work of coordination of the units in Lipjan municipality. It was the organisation of the guerrilla units which -- where I fought and which I myself organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, that was a very long speech but it did not answer my question. My question was: During May and June of 1998 you've described these various points that existed in Lapusnik, Kroimire, Petrastica, Fustica, Luznica. My question is: During May and June of 1998 was there any coordination or command above those points, those units? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer with yes or no because this is a long period, May/June, and in May the organisation was different from that of June when the KLA started to be consolidated. In May up to mid-June the unit -- there were the guerrilla units which were located in the villages that I mentioned earlier, whereas after or in mid-June the units were coordinated by myself, the units that I mentioned, Fushtice, Blinaje, and I tried to coordinate the units in Zborce and Pjetershtice, but I encountered major problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So is your testimony that May up to mid-June there was no coordination of the units, the guerrilla units, in the various villages? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no coordination because the guerrilla units were guerrilla units and the only hierarchy above them was the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did that change after mid-June 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With -- when the General Staff began to appoint the commanders of the subzones, there was of course a plan by the general to organise the subzones. But the beginning of this phase, that is the appointment of the commanders of the subzones which were determined on the basis of the municipalities, this marks the new beginning -- the beginning of a new organisation which was difficult to consolidate because of a very severe offensive mounted by the Serb forces in July. Therefore, it was very difficult to have this structure function properly, this subzone structure. So you should bear in mind that the development of these subzones or the guerrilla units was not the same in all the places or all over the territory because it differed. In Drenica it developed at an earlier phase; in Dukagjin, it was the same. But after Drenica -- But it was after Drenica. Whereas in Pastrik area, as it was called later, the development was at a later phase and in Nerodime subzone, too. This is how the form -- how the -- the structure of the KLA developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When would you say that the structure developed in the Pastrik zone. You said it developed at a later time. When?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a given date because the structure of the subzone required human resources, great human resources; therefore the structuring of the other units that would be later called brigades in these subzones was quite a long period fraught with great difficulties. Because at the same time we had to deal with the organisation and with the war and taking care of the civilian population and doing many other things. Therefore, it was very hard, this period, for us and we cannot set a certain date for this. Just the appointment of the commanders of the subzones began in June, whereas the structuring of KLA when was possible very late, maybe in -- also in Pastrik in September or October of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before that occurred in September/October of 1998, was there any coordination of the units or posts that you have described from a higher level or was it only when it was consolidated in September and October of 1998 that that was possible?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units that were formed in Lipjan territory which I mentioned earlier, I began to coordinate their actions at the end of June and beginning of July. In July it was I think the 6th of July I was officially appointed the commander of Nerodime subzone covering Lipjan, Ferizaj, Kacanik, Elez Hani municipalities. In this way I could start the coordination of the actions of these guerrilla units; however, the severe fights which took place in this month, in July, prevented me from continuing this work in the subzone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from that work that you just described in the Nerodimlje zone, were you aware in June or July of any other structure being created that coordinated the various points that we've talked about, Kroimire, Lapusnik, Luznica, Fustica, Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no other structure. I'm talking about the earlier phase of the coordination of the operations of these units at the end of June and the beginning of July. So these units were guerrilla units which operated and which had above them the General Staff. But at the end of June, I'm talking about the subzone where I would be appointed its commander later, that happened at the end of June/beginning of July, that is the beginning of the coordination. In the Pastrik area, the commander was also appointed, the commander of the Pastrik Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Pastrik Operational subzone was appointed Musa Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And during June and July of 1998 do you know what Fatmir Limaj was doing?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection Fatmir Limaj was with the Celiku unit based in Klecke, and he was there with the unit in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what were his duties or responsibilities during June and July of 1998 to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of other responsibilities of Fatmir Limaj, other than the one I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the witness be excused from the courtroom; I have an application to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Buja, there is some matter which counsel has to raise with the Chamber. Would you please wait outside the courtroom while that matter is dealt with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, thank you for waiting. Unfortunately the problem -- or a problem has arisen that Defence counsel have been working on one translation of certain materials, whereas the Prosecution are working on a different one. It directly affects your evidence, and because of that it will be necessary for the Chamber to stop sitting now instead of sitting on for another hour or so to allow time for the translation difficulty to be resolved, which means that we must ask you to return on Monday at 2.15. There will then be some further submissions by Defence counsel, hoping by then that they have overcome the problem of the translation. And once that is resolved, I'm not sure at the moment how long that will take, but in the course of Monday afternoon you will be recalled to continue your evidence. We apologise for this delay, but it means your evidence will take a little longer than before. But these difficulties, as you will understand, have to be resolved in fairness to the accused people. So we propose to adjourn now to resume the hearing of this trial at 2.15 on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
